extraction.name: MVBench
extraction.description: A comprehensive Multi-modal Video understanding Benchmark covering 20 challenging temporal-related video tasks ranging from perception to cognition that cannot be effectively solved with a single frame. Guided by static-to-dynamic task definitions, public video annotations are automatically converted into multiple-choice QA pairs using LLMs.
extraction.creator: Kunchang Li, Yali Wang, Yinan He, Yizhuo Li, Yi Wang, Yi Liu, Zun Wang, Jilan Xu, Guo Chen, Ping Luo, Limin Wang, Yu Qiao
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Videos and annotations are collected from 11 public video benchmarks (STAR, PAXION, Moments in Time V1, FunQA, CLEVRER, Perception Test, Charades-STA, MoVQA, NTU RGB+D, VLN-CE, and TVQA) covering diverse domains and scenes (first-person and third-person, indoor and outdoor). The dataset applies filtration based on temporal sensitivity (eliminating short clips with negligible motion and extremely long videos, retaining durations primarily between 5s and 35s) and question difficulty, producing 200 multiple-choice QA pairs per task across 20 temporal tasks (totaling 4,000 QA pairs).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: 11 public video datasets: STAR, PAXION, Moments in Time V1 (MiT V1), FunQA, CLEVRER, Perception Test, Charades-STA, MoVQA, NTU RGB+D, VLN-CE, and TVQA.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Videos were filtered by duration (primarily 5s to 35s). For STAR, start or end points were randomly shifted to balance question difficulty. For CLEVRER, questions requiring more than 10 conditions were excluded. Option order was randomly shuffled, 3 to 5 answer options were randomly sampled from candidates, and LLMs were used to ensure options had similar and reasonable text lengths to prevent answer leakage.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Automatic QA generation was guided by task definitions. ChatGPT was used to generate questions based on the task definition when necessary, while answer options were generated either via template-based construction directly from ground-truth annotations (e.g., Action Antonym, Moving Direction) or via LLM-based generation (e.g., converting open-ended QAs in Unexpected Action into multiple-choice).
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Full results and benchmark updates are hosted at https://huggingface.co/spaces/OpenGVLab/MVBench_Leaderboard and models/data are at https://github.com/OpenGVLab/Ask-Anything.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The benchmark design utilizes multiple-choice questions grounded in ground-truth video annotations specifically to avoid the biased scoring of LLMs that occurs in open-ended evaluations.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Current MLLMs encounter difficulties with position, counting, and character-related tasks due to lack of exposure or grounding data. Visual information alone is insufficient for complex cognition tasks (such as TVQA episodic reasoning and egocentric navigation), which may require incorporation of speech/subtitles, depth, or audio.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing/evaluation benchmark for assessing temporal understanding capabilities of Multi-modal Large Language Models (MLLMs).
